analysis:
MARKET REGIME: SPY in confirmed uptrend (+2.5% vs SMA50, slope +0.82%). Conditions support selective new exposure but discipline around quality and entry timing remains paramount given our poor historical profit factor (0.55x) and negative Sortino ratio (-1.72). We cannot afford sloppy entries.

EXISTING POSITION REVIEW:
- AMP (+4.05%): Thesis intact. Financial services quality compounder, momentum healthy. Hold.
- LMT (+3.23%): Defense thesis intact, geopolitical tailwinds, sector performing. Hold.
- MCO (+5.49%): Best performer; Moody's credit ratings franchise — durable moat, compounding nicely. Hold.
- TEL (-5.03%): FLAGGED. Price at $204.26 vs entry $215.07, now trading BELOW SMA50 and SMA200. At 2x ATR (~$6.30) below original entry the stop would be ~$202. We are testing that level now. The fundamental thesis (connector/electrification, fwd P/E 15.77, PEG 0.88, 13.8% revenue growth) remains intact, but trend is MIXED/SIDEWAYS. Monitor daily — if TEL closes below $202, honor the stop and exit. Do not average down. The position has not technically stopped out yet, but it is on watch.

NEW TRADE RATIONALE: One new position is appropriate given $23,238 headroom and room for a 5th slot. IDXX (IDEXX Laboratories) stands out as the highest-quality setup in the screened list: exceptional moat (veterinary diagnostics recurring revenue), ROE 74%, 35% operating margin, $909M FCF, only 15% into its 52-week range (deep Stage 1/2 transition territory), and barely reclaiming SMA50 (+0.2%) with SMA50 slope turning positive. This is the textbook 'basing knife, not falling knife' entry. Valuation is premium (fwd P/E 33.6) but justified for this quality tier. Earnings are 74 days out, providing a safe holding window. All other high-ranked candidates either are too extended above SMA50 (IT +28%, CTSH +24.9%, ADBE +17.8%), have near-term earnings risk (LULU 14d, ADBE 21d), show declining EPS revisions (HCA -2.9%, AOS -1.8%), or represent sector overlap (HII vs LMT). Adding IDXX brings total deployment to ~92%, within the 95% gross cap.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit order at $562 or better on a slight intraday pullback to the SMA50 zone. If price gaps above $570 on open, wait for a retest of SMA50 before initiating.
trades.rationale: FUNDAMENTAL: IDEXX is among the highest-quality businesses in the S&P 500. Veterinary diagnostics is a sticky, recurring-revenue model — pet owners do not defer cancer screenings for dogs the way they delay elective procedures for themselves. ROE of 74.2%, operating margin 35%, FCF $909M, and 9.7% revenue growth justify a premium multiple. Fwd P/E 33.6 is not cheap, but this is a wide-moat compounder that has historically traded at 40-60x. At 15% into its 52-week range after pulling back from $766, we are buying quality at a meaningful discount to recent highs. EPS revisions are modestly positive (+1.3% over 60d). TECHNICAL: Price is re-crossing the SMA50 (currently +0.2%) after a prolonged basing period below both SMAs. SMA50 slope has turned positive at +1.1%. The 52-week range position of 15% is Stage 1/2 transition territory — exactly where Weinstein's methodology calls for entries. ATR(14) at 3.8% is healthy volatility, not excessive. Stop at 2x ATR (~$42.70 below entry, 7.6%) places us below the recent basing low, giving the position room to breathe while keeping portfolio heat under 1.5%.
trades.exit_plan: Primary stop: $519.50 (2x ATR below entry, hard stop). Target: $650 based on partial mean-reversion toward 52-week high. Thesis-break conditions: SMA50 slope turns negative AND price closes back below SMA50 for 3+ consecutive days; or revenue growth decelerates below 5% in next earnings report (Nov 2, 74 days out); or new competitive entrant disrupts veterinary diagnostics pricing. Time stop: If price has not made progress toward $600 within 90 days with no thesis improvement, reassess. Do not hold through earnings if in a loss position.
